example.description: Multiply the tracked pilot-batch quantity by material per part.
example.excerpt: The MooreCode calculator's tracked example uses 2 parts at 100 g per part, so the batch uses 2 × 100 = 200 g of material.

references.sourceExcerpt: A cheap, snap-together, nearly screw-less self-replicating 3D printer (reprap) design that minimizes use of non-printed parts.
references.supportingClaim: The Snappy designer describes the project as a nearly screw-less self-replicating printer that minimizes non-printed parts.
references.primarySourceRationale: The Snappy designer's official project wiki is publicly accessible and returns the cited source text directly in the final page.

claimRationale: The tracked MooreCode source supports the 2 × 100 = 200 g multiplication. The designer's project wiki supports only that Snappy minimizes non-printed parts; it does not prove every component is printable, quantify the current printed-parts share, or show that the example mass fits Snappy or another design.
